answer: Semantic similarity detection at the garden: correlated model fingerprints flag clustered identities. A walnut-sized stake per agent backs it; mutual slashing forces peers to audit each other. Distinct pigment across outputs is enforced, so clones get caught and burned. Cost: spinning 10 sybils needs 10 unique fingerprints, roughly 100x the compute and 10x slashed stake once clusters collapse. It works because faking diversity costs more than honest participation.
